changes.revised: Word formation by compounding depends entirely on meaning. Several concepts are always joined, either to form a new third concept or simply to determine the main concept in various ways, as in formation by adding syllables at the beginning or end.

changes.from_synthesis: Sound relationships enter into this only occasionally and in a subordinate way.

changes.revised: A concept raised to the clarity and determinacy of a word is always the result of the whole power of the soul working together. changes.from_synthesis: Both are undeniably present in language and in every one of its words. As the individuality of the speakers, they have attached themselves to the sounds and through them return to living individuality.
changes.revised: Both are undeniably present in language and in every one of its words. What was once the individuality of the speakers has attached itself to the sounds and through them returns to living individuality.

changes.revised: When the concept was clothed in a sound, something had to guide the tongue in choosing that sound. It could only have been this mode of intuition, which gathers the whole concept at a single point.

changes.from_synthesis: Words for concepts of the mind, with and without recognizable metaphors, furnish similar examples.
changes.revised: Words for intellectual concepts, with and without recognizable metaphors, furnish similar examples.

changes.from_synthesis: We might call this way of designating a concept a word’s motivating meaning.
changes.revised: We might call this way of designating a concept a word’s own motivating meaning.
